issue_context.title: Allow onRoute to alter options without side effects
issue_context.body:
## 🚀 Feature Proposal

The way the `onRoute` hook can be used is to derive some info from the route settings (for swagger for example), or to __mutate the route definition itself__. However in certain cases Fastify creates two routes from the same definition  (see https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/834a4e58de86d7996b50a4663fbf2b0fac4686ee/lib/route.js#L163-L170).

I propose to update the `onRoute` hook so that:

```js
fastify.addHook('onRoute', function (opts) {
  const copy = Object.assign({}, opts)
  copy.onRequest = newHook
  return copy
})
```

This is to avoid having some custom state like in: https://github.com/fastify/fastify-compress/pull/141.

Note that the actual change is quite simple, as we just need to alter:
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/834a4e58de86d7996b50a4663fbf2b0fac4686ee/lib/route.js#L200-L207.

This change is semver-major and should target the `next`  branch.
comments: This is another example of this problem: https://github.com/fastify/fastify-rate-limit/issues/120.

can we just remove the second `afterRouteAdded.call`  here in line 168 
🤔

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/834a4e58de86d7996b50a4663fbf2b0fac4686ee/lib/route.js#L163-L170

> can we just remove the second afterRouteAdded.call here in line 168

Unfortunately no. That's needed to support the `ignoreTrailingSlash` option.

Moreover, it would still be a bug, consider the following case:

```js
const opts = {
  onRequest: [...]
}
fastify.post('/', opts, handler)
fastify.put('/', opts, handler)
```

You'd see the exact same problem.

I'd like to work on this @mcollina, can you clarify the desired behavior for me?

You mentioned that a copy of the route options is created using `Object.assign`, but what happens next?
Should that copy be used to create the context and register the route on the router? In this case we'd be trying to register X new routes from the same original route definition (where X is the number of `onRoute` hooks executed, which btw wouldn't have necessarily mutated the route definition)

> I'd like to work on this @mcollina, can you clarify the desired behavior for me?
> 
>

I would leave this to the implementor of the hook. It might just be 2 levels (main object and hooks), or a partial tree.

I'm having a look at this and wondering if there isn't an existing fundamental issue in the handling of the trailing slash.

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/834a4e58de86d7996b50a4663fbf2b0fac4686ee/lib/route.js#L163-L170

If the conditional is entered, we have two async operations calling the same callback, right? I understand it may not in practice lead to big issues, but it doesn't look right either.
@simoneb Actually there will have two routes: `/path` and `/path/`.

> @simoneb Actually there will have two routes: `/path` and `/path/`.

Yes I can see that, but both are calling the same `done` callback.

> I'm having a look at this and wondering if there isn't an existing fundamental issue in the handling of the trailing slash.
> 
> 
> 
> https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/834a4e58de86d7996b50a4663fbf2b0fac4686ee/lib/route.js#L163-L170
> 
> 
> 
> If the conditional is entered, we have two async operations calling the same callback, right? I understand it may not in practice lead to big issues, but it doesn't look right either.

That's correct and expected. That's how we support the trailing slash.

I guess I'm missing something then, I don't understand how calling the `done` callback twice is correct. I tried tracing back to where that callback comes from and it's buried somewhere in the avvio package so I lost track of how it's handled. Conceptually, that callback is used to communicate to the caller that the async operation is completed and the caller may be waiting for that before continuing doing something else, so calling it twice doesn't seem right to me but I appreciate I may be missing context.
@simoneb only one route will be hit for a request. So the `done` is only invoked once per route handled. `'/foo' == '/foo/'` in terms the handler.

It looks like I'm not explaining myself. This is not something that happens when the routes are hit, but when they are registered.

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/834a4e58de86d7996b50a4663fbf2b0fac4686ee/lib/route.js#L163-L170

This causes the `done` callback to be called twice. I traced it back to [this function in avvio](https://github.com/fastify/avvio/blob/24c4ff1d163f8264d8714dfe9ca6d0b215cbd009/boot.js#L452-L462).

You can see that in the else branch nothing's done. If that function was modified to set the timer to null when it's cleared and throw an exception if timer is null, then under the conditions of this issue (two routes registered), you'll get an exception because the `done` callback is called twice.

Now this may not be a big issue, that callback is notifying avvio that the plugin has finished registering, but in this case it's signalling that it's finished registering after the first route is registered, while the second still has to be registered. I don't know what kind of consequences this may have, but I guess some code waiting for the full registration of the plugin may not work correctly.

I appreciate this may be a kind of extreme edge case though.

I'd like to present my take on the original issue.

The way we prevented acting twice in https://github.com/fastify/fastify-compress/pull/141 was by adding a property to the `routeOptions`. However, if we somehow knew in `onRoute` if it's being called for the same route as before but just for prefixing a slash then we'd be able to avoid adding custom property right?

How do you guys feel if we get a `routeOptions.prefixing` property?

```js
fastify.addHook('onRoute', (routeOptions) => {
  console.log(routeOptions.prefixing) // true when relevant
})
```

With this `fastify-compress` could detect when not to act.

Let me know what you think.

I might be wrong, but for me, the hook is working properly since it adds two routes when `ignoreTrailingSlash = true`. But yeah, the use case is a bit complex.

I would change to a different approach, instead of adding a property to identify if the route has the same handler as others. How complex should be register the route only once but on lookup we transform `/path/` to `/path`? I mean, this is only an idea to fix the problem above, not sure if it's related to the current issue, I would create a new issue for that though.

> I would change to a different approach, instead of adding a property to identify if the route has the same handler as others. How complex should be register the route only once but on lookup we transform /path/ to /path

This will slow us down :(

review_comments: This is not mapping 1:1 to the compress case. Could you add _another_ onRequest hook (not replacing it).

My understanding of that issue is that for `fastify-compress` the `onRoute` is called twice and the `onSend` hook is added twice to the route definition. This results in doubly-compressed response data.

My fix here bypasses that and ensures that the the `onSend` hook is only added once.
Anyway, I will update the test to add another onRequest hook.

Also, the issue I mentioned in Salman's PR happens here too in some cases, will provide a fix for it as well.
I mean that you should test if an `onRoute` hook is already present and `onRoute` receives an array.

> I mean that you should test if an `onRoute` hook is already present

Do you mean test if an `onRequest` hook is already present? If not, how would I check if an `onRoute` hook is already present? AFAIK the route definition doesn't contain `onRoute` hooks.

> and `onRoute` receives an array.

The test I added does show that it received an `onRequest` array.

Here's what happens. The test contains two `onRoute` hooks:
- The first one makes sure that `onRequest` is `undefined` then sets it.
- The second makes sure that it receives an `onRequest` array with one element (set by the previous hook)

This displays that:
- `onRoute` hooks are a reduce operation where they can all mutate the route options and only the last is registered
- route options mutated by `/v1` `onRoute` hooks are not passed to `/v1/` hooks

With that said, I like the solution provided by salman more because it makes sense from an end user perspective that `onRoute` hooks would be called only once for `/v1` and reuse the mutated route options for `/v1/`, so feel free to close this PR if you agree.
